Present Perfect: Review
Let's review the Present Perfect tense.
You use the Present Perfect to:

1. Talk about recent events, with no definite time

For example:
We have just bought a new car.

1. Talk about events that happened at some unknown or unmentioned time in the past

For example:
I have been to Cuba three times.

1. Talk about past events that have a connection to the present

For example:
I don't want to see that movie. I've already seen it.

1. Talk about things which began in the past and are still true

For example:
I have lived here for ten years.

1. Talk about a habitual action that has been occurring frequently up to the present

For example:
I have been working out recently.

Relative Clauses: Review
You use relative clauses to give extra information about someone or something. By combining sentences using relative clauses, your text becomes less repetitive and more concise.
There are two types of relative clauses: “Defining” and “Non-Defining”.
Defining Relative Clauses:
A “Defining Relative Clause” tells you which specific person or thing you are talking about.
For example:

The kid who delivers the newspaper wanted a tip.
The newspaper which the kid delivers is called “The Times”.
The bike that he rides is red.
Non-Defining Relative Clauses:
A “Non-Defining Relative Clause” tells you extra information regarding the person or thing you are talking about. This information is usually not essential.

images.text: I remember a particularly interesting dive that I was hired to do with two other divers whose names I have forgotten since then. We were flown to St. Kitts, which is a tiny island, with all our diving gear and whatever else was needed. It took us three days to locate the shipwreck of “The Explorer”. When we started on the third day of diving we were in raging waters trying to find out what had caused the ship to sink.  The insurance claim on the ship  might have been a fraud. When we examined the ship we began to think it must have been sunk on purpose.

We understood that the owner of the ship, who was a man in his fifties, had recently been divorced and needed to pay child support. He must have needed more money we concluded. One bit of evidence that convinced us was that there was no cargo aboard the ship. If there had been we might have believed it was an accident.
Aboard the ship everything was pristine except where the hull meets the waterline there was a large hole which on first glance could have been made by crashing into a rock. It was hard to decipher because the sea was rough. However, on closer inspection, it was apparent that at the edge of the hole there were drill marks that could only have been made for the purpose of sinking the ship. The suspicion was confirmed!

That was lucky because as we were ascending we felt a tremor. It dawned on me that we were experiencing an earthquake. When we surfaced, it was raining heavily. We had to get ashore and take cover. Luckily it was a mild earthquake that only measured 4 on the Richter Scale. It could have been much worse. For years I have wanted to go back to diving but I've already been awarded with a badge for recovering the Titanic. I've often thought that nothing will beat that experience.
